The Peoples Democratic Party in Ekiti State has called on the police and other security agencies to investigate the alleged attack on its 2026 deputy governorship candidate, Deji Ogunsakin, with a view to arresting and prosecuting the perpetrators and sponsors. The PDP State Chairman, Tunji Odeyemi, who condemned the alleged attack on Ogunsakin, expressed concern over what he termed “growing political intolerance and attacks on members and supporters of opposition parties members”. Odeyemi, a former acting governor of the state, spoke in Ado Ekiti on Monday and charged security agencies and the state government to guarantee the safety of opposition members. Policemen were said to have repelled an alleged attack on Ogunsakin’s house, the venue of a meeting of PDP members and supporters, on Wednesday last week. Describing intolerance and attacks on opposition members as a threat to democracy, Odeyemi said, “The security agencies should get to the root of the attack on Ogunsakin and others. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Ekiti State PDP condemns in the strongest terms these cowardly attacks. There is no justification for violence against any Nigerian citizen for being in or supporting any political party. Democracy dies when opposition is silenced by violence”. He called on the police, Department of State Services and other security agencies to take urgent measures to prevent a recurrence, saying, “Security agencies must act before the situation results in further injuries or loss of lives. “We cannot wait for another attack, another injury or another loss of life before action is taken. Prevention is better than condolence. Attacks on political opponents and the disruption of political gatherings are unacceptable in a democracy. The police, DSS and other relevant authorities must act swiftly”. The PDP chairman called for a level playing field for all political parties, saying, “It is the duty of government to protect and guarantee the safety of everyone, whether in the ruling All Progressives Congress, the PDP, Allied Peoples Movement, or any other political party. Protection must not be selective”. Speaking on the incident, Ogunsakin commended the Ekiti State Commissioner of Police and other officers for their intervention, saying their presence prevented the situation from degenerating. He said, “If not for the police, I probably would not have been here today. When someone was trying to send about 50 people to somebody else’s house to attack people while they were holding their meeting, who knows what would have happened if the police were not on ground? I have petitioned the Commissioner of Police over the incident and copied the state government”. Ogunsakin urged political parties to embrace issue-based campaigns rather than resort to intimidation and violence, insisting that opposition members had the right to participate in political activities without fear. “We (PDP) are opposition forces in this state, and we will not be silenced. Nobody will drive us out of our state or stop us from playing our politics the way we want to play it,” he said. Abiodun Nejo
